The Wall Street Journal reports that Apple has been actively negotiating content deals worth up to nine-figure sums, hoping to improve Siri AI's ability to obtain the latest news and information. Details are as follows.

Apple negotiating with publishers for Siri AI collaboration

According to a report published by The Wall Street Journal today, Apple has been actively approaching publishers, hoping to sign multi-year agreements that would allow Siri AI to access current events and information.

The report content is as follows:

Apple's move comes at a time when publishers, when dealing with AI companies, are increasingly inclined to choose between "court litigation" and "licensing content." For example, The New York Times is currently suing OpenAI and Microsoft in court over the alleged unauthorized use of its works to train AI models; while publishers such as News Corp and Axel Springer have chosen to reach content licensing agreements with the maker of ChatGPT.

Reddit has also tried both approaches. On one hand, it reached an agreement with Google in 2024 (still under review), reportedly worth approximately US$60 million per year, licensing its content for AI training; on the other hand, it has also separately sued Anthropic and Perplexity, accusing them of scraping its data without authorization.

Returning to The Wall Street Journal report, the article points out that such deals are not new for Apple, as the company is already working with publishers on Apple News+, and has previously reached agreements including licensing the use of publisher content for its own AI training.

The Wall Street Journal has contacted Apple regarding the matter, but Apple declined to comment.
